text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementZoologyThe Temperamental Nature of Alligator Gender-Reveal PartiesWith just a degree or two determining gator sex ratiosDRBy Devin Reese9:00 AM CST on November 11, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleHuman embryos grow at a comfortable temperature just a bit warmer than the mother’s body. Reptile embryos, however, are at the whim of outside temperatures. And, in many cases, the sex of the offspring is known to be decided by incubation temperature.  Powered By 1060.3K 10ShareNextStayIn fact, a recent study published in the Journal of Experimental Biology found that the sex of American alligators (Alligator mississippiensis) is set by just a one- or two-degree difference.
